title: Will and Alibi
premise: Estate lawyer Mara Galloway is handed a will naming a beneficiary who died twelve years ago — the same night the town of Harrow's Bend buried its secrets along with a girl named Ivy Lark. When a stranger is found dead wearing clothes lifted from Mara's own closet, the police fix on Mara as their prime suspect, and the only defense is finding the 'dead' witness everyone swears no one ever saw. As the annual Founders' Dinner approaches, Mara uncovers that Ivy faked her death to escape a conspiracy involving the town's founding families — and that the will was planted to force someone to dig. In the end, Mara finds Ivy alive in hiding, exposes the killer among the dinner guests, and must choose between protecting the town's fragile peace and telling a truth that will burn it down; she chooses truth, and love, over duty.
about_author: August Reyes is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade watching ordinary people sign away extraordinary truths. They write mysteries about paper trails, quiet towns, and the lies communities agree to keep.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Mara Galloway opens a sealed envelope delivered to her firm: a notarized will dated the night Ivy Lark drowned, leaving everything to a witness described only as 'the one who saw.' POV: Mara. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into personal dread as she recognizes the notary's stamp — her own late father's.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Mara searches her father's old case files and finds Ivy's estate suspiciously thin — a single page missing from the coroner's packet. Flashbacks establish her twelve years of keeping Harrow's Bend tidy for its powerful families. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the first crack in the identity she built on order and silence.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: A stranger is found dead on the riverbank dressed head-to-toe in garments stolen from Mara's closet, including a monogrammed scarf. Detective Sana Okafor arrives, sharp and skeptical. POV: alternating Mara and Okafor. Emotional beat: fear — Mara realizes someone is staging her into a story.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Okafor interviews Mara, who admits she notarized documents connected to Ivy's death but claims ignorance of details. The town begins whispering. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: Okafor's instinct that Mara is both suspect and fellow investigator — duty pulling against sympathy.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Invitations go out for the Founders' Dinner marking twelve years since Ivy's drowning. Mara notices every attendee's family benefited from Ivy's estate settlement. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the will wasn't an accident; it was an invitation.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Mara and her estranged brother Theo, a local journalist, dredge old records and find a second autopsy report suppressed by Judge Calloway, their uncle. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: sibling resentment thawing into uneasy alliance as shared guilt surfaces.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: A retired deputy, drunk and terrified, tells Mara he drove a living girl out of town the night after the funeral — but won't say who paid him. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: vertigo; if Ivy lives, then Mara's whole career of settled estates is built on a corpse that walked away.

chapters.title: Closet Thief
chapters.summary: Security footage shows the dead stranger entering Mara's house weeks earlier with a key. Someone inside her circle let him in. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: betrayal — the investigation turns inward toward Mara's closest people.

chapters.title: Dinner Reservations
chapters.summary: Judge Calloway pressures Mara to declare the will fraudulent and close the file before the anniversary. He offers her his seat on the family trust. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: temptation — the comfortable lie versus the dangerous truth, love of family against duty to the dead.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Theo finds unsent letters in Ivy's old locker addressed to 'M.' — possibly Mara's mother, who left town the same year. The letters reference a fire at the mill that killed two workers. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: grief reframed; the past is bigger and crueler than anyone filed away.

chapters.title: Someone Follows the Paper
chapters.summary: Mara's office is ransacked; only the will and the missing coroner page are taken. She realizes the killer is cleaning the trail she's following. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: isolation hardening into resolve — she makes copies and hides them where only she would look.

chapters.title: The Deputy Recants
chapters.summary: Before Okafor can formally interview him, the retired deputy dies in an apparent accident — brakes failed on the mill road. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: fury and urgency; the killer is ahead of them, and the clock is now the dinner date.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Glass Raising
chapters.summary: At a memorial service, Mara watches the founding families toast Ivy's memory and catches Judge Calloway's hand trembling around his glass. A note slides into her pocket: STOP ASKING WHO SAW. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: dread made intimate — the threat knows her movements.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Graphology confirms the will's witness clause and the threatening note share handwriting with Mara's long-gone mother, Ruth. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: heartbreak — the person she loved most may be orchestrating her destruction, or protecting her the only way she knew how.

chapters.title: The Mill Fire File
chapters.summary: Theo publishes a cautious piece on the mill fire; within hours, the newspaper's archive burns. Arson points to someone with a key — the same key cut for Mara's house. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror and defiance; going public has painted a target on both siblings.

chapters.title: Okafor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Okafor's superiors push to arrest Mara for the riverside murder; evidence keeps arriving too neatly. She stalls, secretly convinced Mara is being framed by someone inside the department or courthouse. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: loneliness of principle — choosing the truth over her badge's safety.

chapters.title: The House on Fenwick Road
chapters.summary: Following a postmark from the will's envelope, Mara finds a shuttered cottage and signs someone has lived there for years. On the table: photographs of Mara at every age, kept like a vigil. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: awe and fear colliding — someone has been watching over her all along.

chapters.title: Ivy
chapters.summary: Ivy Lark steps out of the dark: alive, scarred, hiding under Ruth's protection since the night she witnessed the mill fire arson — set by the founding families to erase debts. Ruth sent the will to force the truth open before she died. POV: Ivy. Emotional beat: catharsis — twelve years of silence finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Frame Completes Itself
chapters.summary: Ivy's cottage is torched; Mara and Ivy barely escape, but planted evidence names Mara for both deaths. Okafor must choose between the warrant in her hand and the pattern she can finally see. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: crisis of duty — she hides Ivy and declares the warrant flawed, burning her career to keep the case alive.

chapters.title: The Founders' Dinner
chapters.summary: Mara walks into the anniversary dinner wearing a wire, seating herself beside Judge Calloway. She reads the will aloud as a toast, forcing the room to react while Okafor records. Calloway breaks, confessing the fire cover-up and the staged death — and reveals the riverside killer acted alone to protect him. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: climax — terror transfigured into triumph as glass shatters and handcuffs click.

chapters.title: What Duty Owes the Dead
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Mara probates Ivy's real will, restoring the stolen estate to the mill fire victims' families. Her uncle faces trial; her mother's letters are finally read aloud. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: mourning and release — justice costs her the family name, and she pays it willingly.

chapters.title: Will and Alibi
chapters.summary: One year later, Mara reopens her practice with a new sign and a new partner: Ivy, studying law. Okafor visits with cold coffee and warmer news. The last scene mirrors the first — an envelope arrives — but this time Mara opens it smiling. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: resolution — identity rebuilt not on secrets filed away, but on truths told together.
